newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close higher, LVMH rebounds.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close higher, LVMH rebounds.

text.p: French stocks rose sharply on Friday as investors gave the new Socialist-led government the benefit of the doubt after what was viewed as a prudent keynote policy speech by Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on Thursday.
The CAC-40 index closed up 17.41 points, or 0.64 percent, at 2,757.10. The CAC-40 June futures contract rose 19 to 2,749.

"The markets keep giving Jospin the benefit of the doubt," said a broker. He added that the speech contained no unpleasant surprises, although many questions were left unanswered, notably on how the government would finance its spending plans.
On the week, the CAC finished down 1.83 percent.
"There are some who think the market could fall and others who don't feel there's much to worry about," a trader said.
The bourse was underpinned on Friday by the firmness in the dollar and franc, gains in Frankfurt and an early rise on Wall Street.
Shares in retail and building groups rose on the government's measures to boost consumption and provide more housing.
The CAC index was also boosted by a rebound in luxury goods group LVMH, whose stock finished up 4.79 percent, recovering the ground lost since it began buying up Grand Metropolitan stock this week.

Some analysts sympathise with LVMH Chairman Bernard Arnault's criticisms of the planned merger between Grand Met and Guinness, but others are concerned, saying he risks taking on a lot of debt in his effort to thwart the deal. Arnault is now the biggest shareholder in both the British companies.
